match.reason: The closest bank point, market research for a new business, covers why to research before opening, but not the difference between primary and secondary data that this Year 12 point teaches.

draft.title: Market research
card: Market research is collecting and analysing data to understand customers and the market. A business uses it to make better marketing decisions.
data gathered first-hand by the business or someone it hires, for its own purpose. Surveys, interviews, focus groups and observation are examples.
data that already exists because someone else collected it earlier. Industry reports, Australian Bureau of Statistics figures and a business's own past sales records are examples.
Primary data is usually more specific to the question but costs more time and money. Secondary data is usually cheaper and faster but may be out of date or not fit the question.
draft.remember: Primary data is collected first-hand for the question. Secondary data was collected earlier by someone else.

a.q: Which of these is an example of primary data?
opts: A café owner interviews 30 customers about a new menu
A café owner reads a published report on coffee trends
A café owner reviews last year's sales records
A café owner uses census figures on local incomes
a.why: Interviewing customers gathers new data first-hand for the owner's own question. The other three use data that already existed, which makes it secondary, even the owner's own sales records.
a.clue: Which one means collecting new data from people now?

b.q: Priya plans to open a gym in Wagga Wagga. She downloads a free industry report on gym memberships across NSW. What is the main drawback of this data for her plan?
opts: It may be out of date or not specific to Wagga Wagga
It is gathered first-hand, so it takes too long
It costs more than surveying local residents
It is primary data, so it may be biased
b.why: The report is secondary data. It was collected earlier by someone else for another purpose, so it may be dated or too broad for one town. The report is not first-hand, and secondary data is usually cheaper, not dearer.
b.clue: Think about who collected the report and why.

a.best: A café owner interviews 30 customers about a new menu

b.best: It may be out of date or not specific to Wagga Wagga

problems.detail: The card defines secondary data as data 'someone else collected earlier', then gives 'a business's own past sales records' as an example. Secondary data is data that already exists, collected earlier for another purpose, and it can be collected by the business itself (internal secondary data). The definition contradicts its own example.

'Secondary data was collected earlier by someone else' is too narrow. A business's own past records are secondary data too, so the line contradicts the card's own example. Better: 'collected earlier for another purpose'.

Why (a) calls the owner's own sales records secondary. That is correct, but it contradicts the card's and the remember line's definition ('someone else collected it'), so a student following the card could judge that option to be neither primary nor secondary.

check.summary: Both questions work and the answers are sound. However, the card and the remember line define secondary data as collected 'by someone else', which clashes with their own example of a business's past sales records. Reword to 'collected earlier for another purpose'.
